questions.question: Which cloud benefit ensures that resources are deployed and maintained according to company standards and regulatory requirements?

options.why: Elasticity is about scaling with demand.

questions.explanation: Governance covers rules, templates, auditing and enforcement of standards.

questions.scenario: Your company requires that Azure resources can only be created in two specific regions.
questions.question: Which Azure service should you use to enforce this?

options.why: Correct. An 'Allowed locations' policy denies other regions.
RBAC controls who can act, not where resources go.
Advisor recommends but does not enforce.

questions.explanation: Azure Policy evaluates and enforces rules such as allowed locations.

questions.question: Which TWO ways does the cloud help with governance and compliance?

options.text: Automatic auditing that flags non-compliant resources
Removing the need for any company rules
options.why: Rules are still required; the cloud helps enforce them.

options.text: Templates that deploy resources already meeting standards
Allowing anyone to create anything with no oversight
options.why: That is the opposite of governance.

questions.explanation: Templates and automated auditing and enforcement make governance easier in the cloud.

questions.question: What is the key difference between Azure Policy and Azure role-based access control (RBAC)?

options.text: Policy controls what properties resources can have; RBAC controls who can perform actions
Policy controls who can sign in; RBAC controls resource regions

options.why: They are different services with different purposes.
RBAC is an Azure authorization system.

questions.explanation: Policy governs resource properties and compliance; RBAC governs user permissions.
